issue: The frozen revalidator scored a packet whose root is a symlink as a pass and executed that linked packet's out-of-tree verify.py; a dangling verify.py symlink made it skip the verifier entirely, so a manifest alone carried the packet to pass.
finding: Commit a5413e5a6 ('reject linked packet roots in the frozen revalidator') only extended manifest_file's ancestry walk; run_verify never inspects packet_dir itself, and its own rule already returns 'verify.py is not a regular file' for a dangling link (scripts/test_revalidate_verify_link.py:41) although main gates on Path.exists(), which follows the link and returns False. The successor reconstruction/tooling/revalidation-qualification/audit.py rejects both shapes.

reproduction.linked_root: mkdir research/linked; ln -s <external> research/linked; research/linked/verify.py exits 0 -> results.json overall 'pass', external verifier executed
reproduction.fixed: overall 'fail', verify output 'packet root is not a real directory', external verifier not executed
reproduction.dangling_verifier: packet/verify.py -> missing.py, valid manifest -> has_verify False, overall 'pass'
reproduction.dangling_fixed: has_verify True, overall 'fail', output 'verify.py is not a regular file'

change.run_verify: reject a linked or missing packet root before lstat-ing verify.py, returning status 'fail'
change.has_verify: os.path.lexists instead of Path.exists, so a dangling verifier entry reaches run_verify's existing admission rule instead of being scored as absent

tests.before: 2 failures against the base script (linked root 'pass' != 'fail'; dangling verifier has_verify False)
tests.after: 3 tests OK in 0.14s, including a real-directory control that still runs its verifier

unchanged: packet contents, manifests and prior audit reports
the full research/ revalidation run is not re-executed
not_claimed: No full revalidation of every research packet is rerun for this packet; the CLI tests exercise the same code path on synthetic packets.
